answer: The hollow cap is upheld at intake and ocean shows the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool as a result cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch regardless of capital it holds, since every participant consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. At most 4 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a kernel tag. That is 33 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
